titleDv: ޤާނޫނު ނަންބަރު 4/2013 (ސިޔާސީ ޕާޓީގެ ޤާނޫނު) އަށް ... ވަނަ އިޞްލާޙު ގެނައުމުގެ ބިލު
summary: This government bill amends the Political Parties Act (Law No. 4/2013). It removes the rule that stops someone who ran in a party primary from then running in the same election in another capacity, such as an independent. It changes how state funding for parties is calculated: the 0.1% to 0.2% range would be measured against the revenue the annual budget expects for that year, not the annual budget itself. It adds a MVR 100,000 fine on a party when someone belonging to it breaks the Act. It also replaces the party registration form printed in the Act with a form based on a template the Elections Commission sets.
whyItMatters: Party primary candidates who lose could run again in the same election by another route, and parties themselves, not only individuals, could be fined when their people break the law. The amount of public money parties receive would be tied to expected state revenue.
keyProvisions: Clause 1 repeals Article 10, which bars a party member who contested the party's primary from standing in that election in any other capacity and tells the Elections Commission to cancel such a candidacy.

Clauses 2 and 3 amend Article 20 so a party applies for registration using a form drawn up to a template set by the Elections Commission under regulations. The form must include the proposed name, address and contact details, details of the people representing the party, and other information set in regulations, limited to what the Commission needs to check under Article 12. The form must be public on the Commission's website.
Clause 4 amends Article 35 so annual state funding for parties is between 0.1% and 0.2% of the revenue estimated in that year's state budget, instead of 0.1% to 0.2% of the annual budget.
Clause 5 amends Article 49(a)(2): anyone breaking another article of the Act still faces a fine of MVR 30,000 to 75,000, and the party that person belongs to would also be fined MVR 100,000.
Clauses 6 and 7 repeal Article 53 and the Schedule, which is the registration form currently printed in the Act.

Clause 8 requires regulations affected by the changes to be made and published in the Gazette within 30 days of the law taking effect. Clause 9 says it takes effect once passed, ratified and published in the Gazette.
whoIsAffected: Political parties and their members and candidates, people forming new parties, and the Elections Commission.
statedReasons: The note says the government wants to change how state budget money is given to parties, make parties share responsibility for breaches by holding the party accountable alongside individuals, and have registration forms follow an Elections Commission template instead of a form in the law.
